passage: Layla had said something cutting to Diego at the party in Buenos Aires, about him always being late, and he had left early. For three days there was silence. She rehearsed a hundred messages. Finally she wrote, "Diego, what I said at the party was unkind. I was stressed and took it out on you, and that was my part. I'm sorry. I'd like to hear how it felt for you, whenever you're ready, no rush." He didn't reply that day. On the fifth day he wrote, "I was really hurt. Can we walk on Sunday?" Layla replied yes, and on the walk she mostly listened, without demanding that things go back to how they were.

qa.q: In which city was the party?
qa.a: The party was in Buenos Aires.

qa.q: What does Layla's message suggest she feels about her part in the fallout?
qa.a: Layla said she was stressed and took it out on Diego, and that her words were unkind. She did not blame him or demand forgiveness.

qa.q: What could Layla do on the walk?
qa.a: Listen to how it felt for Diego, avoid excuses and let Diego decide how fast things repair.

qa.q: How might Diego have felt in the days of silence?
qa.a: Diego was probably hurt and needed time, since he wrote on the fifth day that he was really hurt and asked to walk.

grounding: A young adult reaches out after a fallout, names their part, listens and does not demand instant forgiveness.

passage: In the staffroom of the primary school, Mehak and Sonali had stopped talking after an argument about the timetable, in which Mehak had accused Sonali of being lazy. Days later, in the corridor by the notice board, Mehak said, "Sonali, can I say something? What I said about you being lazy was unfair. I was frustrated, and I blamed you instead of asking. I'm sorry." Sonali crossed her arms and looked away. "I need a bit of time," she said. Mehak's stomach dropped, but she nodded. "Of course. I'm here when you want to talk." Two days later Sonali brought her a cup of tea, and they finally talked it out.

qa.q: Where did Mehak apologise to Sonali?
qa.a: Mehak apologised in the corridor by the notice board.

qa.q: What was Sonali feeling when she crossed her arms?
qa.a: Sonali was probably still hurt or guarded, and asked for a bit of time. Mehak accepted this without pushing.

qa.q: What did Mehak do well in her apology?
qa.a: She named exactly what was unfair, said why without excusing it, and accepted Sonali's need for time.

qa.q: How might Mehak have felt when Sonali asked for time?
qa.a: Mehak probably felt worried and disappointed, as her stomach dropped, but she respected the request and said she was there when Sonali wanted to talk.

grounding: A young adult reaches out after a fallout, names their part, listens and gives the other person time.
